candidate: Web onboarding can create a duplicate workspace and first project after an unconfirmed committed response is retried
method: Independent static counterexample/refutation review of immutable git show sources; no product edits, runtime API, database connection, tests or browser.
scope_limit: A successful first commit followed by transport/JSON delivery failure is the trigger. A failure before the first commit cannot by itself create a duplicate. No claim of duplicate paid work or external provider charges.

candidate_path.step: Onboarding calls post('/v1/tenants', {name,project_name}) without the optional requestKey.
post forwards no Idempotency-Key when requestKey is absent; browser api creates crypto.randomUUID() for each invocation.
clientFetch or clientJson throws CLIENT_RESULT_UNCONFIRMED after a failed write transport/response; it makes one attempt and cannot infer commit status.
AsyncForm catches the failure, displays it and unconditionally clears busy. Its submit button becomes enabled again; no request key or unresolved operation is retained.
Retrying the same form invokes post again and produces a different key; backend replay looks up only actor/action/key, so it executes a fresh effect.
Fresh effect inserts a new tenant UUID, owner membership, wallet and first project, then commits. There is no same-user/same-name reuse condition on this path.

refutation_attempts.hypothesis: The networking layer retries using a stable request key or stores the unconfirmed request.
refutation_attempts.evidence: clientFetch does exactly one fetch and throws a typed unconfirmed-write error; post has an optional explicit key but Onboarding does not supply it. New manual submission constructs a new api call and random key.

refutation_attempts.hypothesis: CSRF validation consumes the first request's token, so the same-session retry is rejected.
refutation_attempts.evidence: Browser api supplies the existing csrfToken. Backend compares the supplied token to csrf(db,cookie) for the current valid session, with no consumption or tenant-create-specific rotation. A second valid request passes the same check.

refutation_attempts.hypothesis: Session generation invalidation prevents the retry after the first request.
refutation_attempts.evidence: api rejects a response if the sign-in generation changed; /v1/tenants neither changes the session generation nor signs the user out on an unconfirmed connection result. This guards identity changes, not repeated writes within the same session.

refutation_attempts.hypothesis: Workspace context refresh navigates the user away before retrying.
refutation_attempts.evidence: Onboarding saves IDs, calls w.refresh and navigates only after await post returns. A thrown unconfirmed result skips all three. Context also refreshes on visibility changes, but Onboarding only redirects unauthenticated users; it does not leave /welcome merely because memberships exist. A same-page immediate retry is reachable.

refutation_attempts.hypothesis: The per-user authority lock serializes tenant creation and thereby prevents duplicate names.
refutation_attempts.evidence: lockUserAuthorities serializes operations on the same user, while currentUserAuthority checks only active status and auth_version. A subsequent serialized request still enters replay with its new key and inserts new rows. Neither function checks existing workspace membership or workspace/project names.

refutation_attempts.hypothesis: Backend replay uses request content hash as a cross-key deduplication key.
refutation_attempts.evidence: The advisory lock and SELECT are keyed by actor/action/key. input_hash is only compared if that exact replay row exists; equal bodies with different keys are independent effects. request_replays primary key is actor_id/action/key.

refutation_attempts.hypothesis: Tenant/project/membership unique constraints or insert triggers reject a same-name retry.
refutation_attempts.evidence: Tenant and project IDs are freshly generated UUID primary keys. Tenant names are not unique; projects have UNIQUE(tenant_id,id), and membership uses PRIMARY KEY(tenant_id,user_id). A new tenant UUID makes every retry independent. Migration search found no same-user tenant-name or project-name uniqueness rule; the project_cloud_workspace insert trigger provisions by new project ID, not user/name.

refutation_attempts.hypothesis: Database transaction rollback undoes the first create when delivery fails.
refutation_attempts.evidence: db.tx commits before returning its result. A browser transport/JSON failure after that commit does not invoke transaction rollback. Rollback applies only to an exception inside db.tx before its successful return.

static_reproduction.preconditions: Valid active user session and CSRF token; browser client remains on /welcome; first request commits successfully.
steps: Submit company A and first project B. Client creates key K1.
Allow POST /v1/tenants to commit, but lose or corrupt its response before browser parsing completes.
AsyncForm shows the unconfirmed-result error and re-enables submit; successful-return ID save/context refresh/navigation did not run.
Submit unchanged fields again. Client creates K2 != K1.
Backend serializes the user, finds no replay under K2, and inserts a second company A and first project B under new IDs.

recommended_boundary: Retain a request identity and immutable input for one pending user-owned onboarding operation and reuse it on retry/recovery. Do not impose a global workspace-name uniqueness policy merely to compensate for a client request-identity bug. Preserve identity/session invalidation and backend replay behavior.
open_questions: No deliberate response-loss runtime replay was performed by this reviewer; the parent owns integrated verification.
This review does not evaluate the Desktop bridge's idempotency defaults or Extension onboarding; it confirms the browser Web path only.
